Arecaceae.key_door: costapalmate Sabal fan leaf + fibrous sheath + unarmed petiole; S. minor vs S. mexicana by subterranean vs aerial stem, costa strength, fibers and fruit size

Smilacaceae.key_door: prickly tendrilled vine + broad 3-5-veined reticulate leaf + dioecious 6-tepaled umbels + berries

Nartheciaceae.key_door: basal rosette + leafless scape + rough/farinose 6-tepaled raceme + half-inferior 3-locular ovary + beaked capsule

joey_private_anchors.role: whole-plant habit / basal leaves / flowering spike

taxonomy_notes: Sabal minor and Sabal mexicana remain accepted and native-range treatments include Texas.
Smilax bona-nox and Smilax tamnoides remain accepted and native-range treatments include Texas.
Aletris aurea remains accepted and native range extends through the southeastern U.S. to Texas.
Current Kew/APG places Aletris in Nartheciaceae, order Dioscoreales; older FNA morphology is presented under a broad Liliaceae treatment and is retained only as morphology/source provenance.
guardrails: Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
Do not identify Sabal from size alone; use stem position and costapalmate leaf architecture.
Do not identify Smilax bona-nox from one variable leaf shape.
Do not copy older broad-Liliaceae family placement for Aletris into the current taxonomy.
